Syndication API truncated the text mid-thread after "coordinate with team members" — full five-paragraph text recovered via fxtwitter.

## Summary

Armstrong describes how he has changed his own way of working over "the last few weeks":

- **Org shape:** one **lead agent per area of focus, running all the time**, with a **chief-of-staff agent that oversees them**. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that "write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members."
- **One queue:** everything he needs to decide or review lands in a **single prioritized queue** — "a simple local web app." Each product review arrives with screenshots and a video demo of the feature. He clears the queue **in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts**. Working from one queue instead of dozens of chats "has cut a lot of mental overhead." The leads also surface ideas he hadn't considered.
- **Judgment distillation:** the system keeps learning his preferences and distilling his judgment into a **"Brian brain"** — recommendations and first drafts improve before they reach him; the explicit goal metric is **fewer corrections per change**.
- **Governance:** "Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment."
- Closes by framing this as the productivity frontier tied to "the economy for agents (agentic finance)" — a Coinbase interest.

## Why it matters

- **This is an external, high-profile validation of the architecture this vault's owner already runs.** "One lead agent per area of focus + a chief-of-staff agent overseeing them" is literally the RD Personal Management org chart (CoS + specialist roster), and the trading company's lead-agent structure. Armstrong's post is evidence the pattern is converging industry-wide, not a bespoke experiment — same convergence family as [[2026-10-25-mardehaym-seven-steps-agentic-org]] (the adoption ladder most orgs never climb).
- **The interesting delta is the interface, not the org.** Armstrong consolidated ALL decision traffic into one prioritized queue with rich evidence attached (screenshots, video demos) and batch-clears it by voice. Our equivalent "queue" is currently split across channels: WhatsApp relay traffic (RDP-30), Telegram, and the Paperclip board's in-review items. A single merged, prioritized review queue is the one idea here worth stealing for the personal company.
- **"Fewer corrections per change" is a clean, measurable north-star** for the preference-distillation flywheel — it puts a number on what our memory/skills loop is for. The "Brian brain" framing (distilled judgment improving first drafts before human review) is the same bet as the vault + agent memory stack.
- **Governance parity:** "every change still goes through human review and security checks" is our draft-and-show posture stated as a principle — [[2026-10-01-pocock-lock-down-agents]] for the security-check half.
- **Skepticism gates:** CEO self-report with zero metrics (no time saved, no cost, no failure modes); "the system keeps learning my preferences" is undemonstrated in-post. He also has a company behind him — staff absorb what agents can't, a luxury a solo operator doesn't have, so the mental-overhead savings don't transfer 1:1. And the closing "agentic finance" pivot means the tweet doubles as Coinbase positioning, not pure practice-sharing. Bookmarks (9k on 774k views — a >1% save rate) say readers file this as a recipe.
